Senses.PreferredTarget: take up a case or saying for public comment
AlternateTargets: bring a case forward for comment
raise and handle an inherited saying
Senses.Note: The same action appears grammatically as a verb, an agent noun, and a label for collected commentarial statements. Twenty-one occurrences of the agent-noun form name people who do the picking up and presenting; they are not direct definitions. The corpus relation to dragging through mud and carrying water is included because Dagui's comment draws it explicitly.

Senses.Explanation: To take up an inherited case, encounter, or saying and bring it before listeners for comment. The action belongs to the public handling of the record: the material is raised, quoted, appraised, or deliberately left without further comment. Wumen Huikai's publication notice calls his book “forty-eight cases taking up and presenting the encounters of buddhas and ancestral teachers” (拈提佛祖機緣四十八則). Jingfu says lineage descendants successively raised and voiced the inherited material and took it up for comment (舉唱之、拈提之); his editorial rules classify the collected material as masters' “statements of taking up and commenting” (諸師拈提語). Yuanwu Keqin uses the verb for a person moving within and bringing forward the upward hinge (向箇裏出沒，向箇裏拈提). Dahui Zonggao puts two opposed statements together “without further taking them up for comment” (更無拈提), leaving students to distinguish them. Yulin Tongxiu says few in the communities had taken up and commented on the old woman's burning-the-hut case (者個公案叢林中少有拈提者). Dagui Huaixiu appraises Baofu Congzhan's handling as having considerable house style, then says that under questioning it again dragged through mud and carried water (保福拈提，頗有宗風，及乎問著，又却拖泥帶水).
